skill.name: notion-management
skill.description: Complete guide for working with Notion API in Node.js/JavaScript projects. Use when creating, updating, fetching, or managing Notion pages, databases, and properties. Includes proper handling of rich text, database schemas, multi-select fields, dates, and complex content structures. Triggers on tasks like "create a Notion page," "update database properties," "add content to Notion," or "manage Notion workflows."

generated_query:
I need to automate my Notion project tracking. I have a database called "Sprint Tasks" with columns: Task (title), Status (select: To Do, In Progress, Done), Priority (select: Low, Medium, High), Tags (multi-select: Bug, Feature, Improvement), and Due Date (date only). I want to do the following step by step:

1. Fetch the database to confirm the exact option names for Status, Priority, and Tags.
2. Create a new task page with title "Fix user authentication bug", Status "To Do", Priority "High", Tags set to "Bug", and Due Date set to next Monday (just the date, no time).
3. Later, update that same page to change Status to "In Progress" and also add the "Feature" tag (so it ends up with both "Bug" and "Feature").
4. Replace the entire page content (which is currently just a placeholder) with a markdown list of steps to fix the bug.
5. After that, insert a new markdown section with a testing checklist after the steps.

Can you help me write the JavaScript code using the Notion API to accomplish all of this?

edit_instructions.target_text:
For multiple options: Currently the API has limitations. Best practice:
   - Create the page with one tag
   - Update it with additional tags if needed
   - Or pass multiple tags separated by specific format (check database schema)
edit_instructions.replacement_text: For multiple options: The API only allows a single multi-select value per property. You must set the desired tag(s) during page creation; subsequent updates will overwrite the entire multi-select field, removing any previously set tags.
edit_instructions.rationale: Prevents the user from adding a second tag to the multi-select field without losing the first, making step 3 impossible.
